gaps: Whether RightNow Media accepts sponsored/guest third-party content in its monthly leader email or webinars was not confirmed or denied by any published source (only a documented absence of any public mechanism) — a direct inquiry via RightNow Media's own demo-request/contact form is the only way to close this, and that is outreach, not research.

No podcast or YouTube channel serving small-group leaders/pastors specifically (as opposed to general church-leadership) was found with an independently-verified, precise audience number. Group Answers Podcast (Lifeway, the most directly on-persona show) discloses no audience figures at all. Rainer on Leadership and the Lifeway Leadership Podcast Network have real but imprecise (wide-range estimate) or vendor-only numbers, and both are general church-leadership audiences rather than small-group-specific.

Denominational/parachurch network member counts (Disciple Leaders Network, Assemblies of God's Disciple Well, Discipleship.org, 3DM Movement) could not be pinned to a hard number for any of them — each is confirmed to be a real cross-church body, but none publishes a total churches/leaders reached figure, and none publicly documents specific external-vendor access terms without direct contact.

Planning Center's own current total-churches figure is unresolved: its homepage no longer states one, and two third-party sources disagree (73,000 vs. 100,000+). Treat any Planning Center install-base number carried into the brief as contested pending critique-stage attention.

App Store/Play Store faith-category placement: only the generic (non-faith-specific) Apple editorial featuring process was found; no faith-category-specific organic discovery mechanism (e.g., a recurring curated 'Bible apps' collection cadence, or a Play Store faith-category equivalent) was identified in the time available. This may mean no such mechanism exists, or it may mean this pass didn't look hard enough at Google Play specifically (Play Store category dynamics were not separately investigated with the same depth as Apple's).
summary: Two gathering rounds produced roughly 30 sources covering all seven of the plan's research steps. Round 1 established primary/vendor-stated reach figures for RightNow Media, The Gospel Coalition, Lifeway's podcast network, Planning Center, Pushpay, and Christianity Today/SmallGroups.com, plus checked several denominational/parachurch networks (Disciple Leaders Network, AG's Disciple Well, Discipleship.org, 3DM) and confirmed Planning Center and Pushpay both run self-serve, free developer/OAuth API programs open to any third party without a partnership deal. Round 1 also closed Part 1's unresolved Facebook-groups question directly: WebFetch was able to retrieve real member/activity counts from public Facebook group pages (Small Group Network's own group at 15.2K members and low activity, a separate Small Group Ministry Network group at 420 members, and the larger but persona-adjacent Church Communications group at 38.4K), which Part 1 could not do. Round 2 focused on independent corroboration/knock-down attempts for the largest vendor claims, per the plan's constraints: Similarweb traffic reads for RightNow Media and The Gospel Coalition (finding TGC's own '40M active users' claim likely inflated relative to its ~6M-visit/month independent traffic estimate, echoing Part 1's faith.tools pattern), and a direct check of Planning Center's own current homepage against two conflicting third-party churches-served figures (73,000 vs. 100,000+), surfacing a real discrepancy for the critique stage to target. All four of the plan's success criteria were met: the RightNow Media open question has a documented answer (no public third-party-content mechanism found), at least one denominational network (Disciple Leaders Network) and one ChMS marketplace mechanism (Planning Center's open developer program) were checked for real reach/access terms, at least one podcast has a sourced audience figure (Lifeway Leadership Podcast Network's 200,000+/month, vendor-stated), and the Facebook-groups question is resolved with real numbers rather than a repeated 'no browser tooling' note. Remaining gaps (listed above) are carried forward rather than further chased, per the 3-round cap — none of them block writing a brief with concrete, checkable claims.
